archetype.name: Dual-Threat (scramble-first)
archetype.definition: A thick-framed runner whose real value comes from breaking the pocket and scrambling for first downs, not from designed runs or a reliable passing game, which so far has worked only in the intermediate middle tier.

report.headline: His legs are keeping Miami afloat; his arm is sinking them.
report.take:
Willis has finally received the starting run his Green Bay cameos seemed to earn, and five starts in, the passing has not held up. His -0.201 EPA per dropback ranks 40th of 45, his CPOE of -7.72 is 40th, and he has 2 touchdown passes against 4 interceptions and 3 lost fumbles in an 0-5 start. What he does well is run. He has 186 rushing yards, fourth among quarterbacks, and 17 scrambles have produced 167 yards, 8 first downs and +0.755 EPA apiece. Miami's coaches know where the value is. The Dolphins pass 11.1 points less often than situation predicts, 31st in the league, and they are clearly working to keep the ball out of his hands.

The passing profile is lopsided. Throws of 10-19 air yards are the one area that works: 27 attempts at +0.465 EPA, adding 12.6 points. Everything around that tier is poor. Throws behind the line have cost 10 points, so the screen and swing game is a net loss. Deep balls are completing at 17.9% with a -20.9 CPOE. He holds the ball (3.17 seconds to throw), and his bad-throw rate of 18.5% ranks 35th of 37. That pairing describes a quarterback who struggles to process in rhythm and then misses when he does pull the trigger. One target is absorbing much of the damage: Kevin Coleman Jr. has drawn 17 targets at -0.73 EPA each, while tight end Greg Dulcich (+0.22 per target) has been his most efficient option.

The numbers hide less than they first appear to. You could blame the schedule, since Weeks 2 through 4 came against SF, KC and MIN, who rank 5th, 3rd and 1st in defensive EPA today. That is fair as far as it goes. But Week 5 came against a mid-pack Cincinnati defense (15th), and he still posted -11.4 passing EPA with two interceptions. Nor is this garbage-time distortion working against him: in one-score games his EPA per play is -0.331 with a -12.6 CPOE, much worse than the -0.13 he posts when trailing by 9 or more. The Green Bay seasons look like the outlier. His 2025 line (85.7% completions, +22 CPOE) came from two games, while his 2022 Tennessee season (-10.6 CPOE, -0.459 EPA per play) looks a lot like this one. One thing does look improved: his pressure-to-sack rate of 31.1% is well below the 60%-plus he ran in Green Bay, and his sack rate has dropped to 5.9% over the last three games.

Going forward, expect a low-volume, run-supported quarterback who can produce fantasy points with his legs but drags down Miami's offense through the air. Unless the intermediate throws start carrying over into the short and deep game, his ceiling as a passer is roughly what he showed at San Francisco in Week 2. That was a conservative, 6.4-intended-air-yard plan and his only positive passing EPA game.

strengths.title: Scrambles that move the chains
strengths.body: When the play breaks down he takes off, and it pays: 17 scrambles have averaged +0.755 EPA with 8 first downs, and his 37.2 rushing yards a game rank third. This is a trait he has carried through every stop of his career, so the production should last, especially with Miami leaning on the run.

strengths.title: Intermediate throws work
strengths.body: The 10-19 yard window is the only part of the passing game adding value: +0.465 EPA per attempt and 12.6 points total, with a positive CPOE. It is a 27-attempt sample, but it shows where the offense can build. More dig and crossing concepts, fewer screens and fewer bombs.

strengths.title: Sack problem easing
strengths.body: His career pressure-to-sack rates ran above 60% in Green Bay. This year that rate is 31.1%, and his sack rate over the last three games is 5.9%, lower than his season figure. Some of that is the Kansas City game, where he was barely pressured. Still, it is the one passing trend moving the right way.

concerns.title: Accuracy is the core flaw
concerns.body: A -7.72 CPOE and an 18.5% bad-throw rate show he misses throws he should complete. The deep ball has collapsed at 17.9% completions. His 2022 Titans season carried the same signature, so this looks like who he is rather than a slump. The Packers numbers came on samples too small to count against it.

concerns.title: The easy throws are costing points
concerns.body: Passes behind the line have lost 10 points of EPA, with a 30.8% success rate, and short throws are below average. In most offenses this layer of the passing game is a safety valve; here it is a drain. Some of that falls on design and receivers, and Coleman's -12.4 EPA stands out. But a quarterback who can't make the layup throws limits the whole playbook.

concerns.title: Ball security, in the hands and out
concerns.body: Three lost fumbles rank 42nd of 45, and he has five fumbles in total alongside four interceptions. The fumbles partly come with a ball-holding, scrambling style, and lost-fumble counts tend to swing with luck. Even so, for a quarterback whose margin is already thin, it costs possessions.

trend.note: His passing has worsened, from +4.5 EPA at San Francisco to -12.4 and -11.4 in Weeks 4 and 5, with last-three EPA per dropback at -0.328. The legs have gone the other way, averaging 47 rushing yards a game over that stretch, including 74 against Cincinnati.

nextGame.headline: Rested, but facing a pass rush built to punish his hold time
nextGame.body:
The Jets are a bad matchup for the parts of his game that work. Their run defense ranks 4th in EPA, and their sack rate of 7.7% ranks 6th, which threatens a quarterback who averages 3.17 seconds to throw. They also allow the 4th-fewest passing yards to quarterbacks. Their weak spot is the short game, 22nd in short-pass EPA, but that is where Willis has been worst, so it may not help much. With the Jets favored by 4.5 and a 38.5 total, the Book expects a low-scoring divisional game. That likely keeps Miami in its run-heavy shell, and that shell is also where his one-score numbers have been worst.

Availability cuts both ways. On Miami's side, guard Jonah Savaiinaea (85% of snaps) was limited Monday with an ankle injury. Losing him against this pass rush would matter more than any skill-position absence, and Caleb Douglas's limited ankle injury could thin out the receiver group further. On the other side, the Jets lose rotational edge Joseph Ossai, a modest break for the protection. Their offense is also without Breece Hall, Adonai Mitchell and guard Dylan Parham, which should keep the score close but tight. Miami also comes off a bye with 14 days of rest.

keyMatchups.title: Jets pass rush vs. his clock
keyMatchups.body: New York gets home at the 6th-best rate in the league, and Willis holds the ball longer than most. If Savaiinaea can't go, the interior gets weaker right when it needs to hold up.

keyMatchups.title: Scrambles against a stout run front
keyMatchups.body: The Jets' 4th-ranked run defense should shut down designed quarterback runs, which have been weak anyway at 1.9 yards a carry. His scramble value comes from broken plays, though, and that is where his fantasy floor lies.

keyMatchups.title: Top options run into strengths
keyMatchups.body: The Jets have held opposing WR1s 4.8 PPR points under their averages and rank 7th against lead tight ends. Those roles belong to Malik Washington, his most-targeted receiver, and Dulcich, his most efficient one.

nextGame.watch: Whether the bye produces a quicker-game plan like Week 2's that gets the ball out before the Jets' rush arrives, or he holds it again and takes sacks.

restOfSeason.body:
The rushing is the sustainable part. Scrambling has been part of his game at every stop, and Miami's run-first approach suits it, so 30-50 yards a game on the ground is a reasonable baseline. The passing is unlikely to bounce back to anything like his Green Bay form. This five-game run is his largest sample, and it matches his 2022 profile. Expect roughly 145 to 190 passing yards a game on low volume, with touchdown passes scarce. His 1.5% touchdown rate should drift up some from bottom-three territory, but it won't get anywhere near league average.

What may regress in his favor: the lost-fumble count, plus a schedule that can't keep offering top-five defenses. What won't: the accuracy, and a Dolphins defense ranked 29th that keeps putting him in catch-up spots he hasn't handled well. His job security is also worth watching. An 0-5 team with a bottom-five passing offense is the setting in which coaches start considering other options, though the dossier gives no sign of a change yet.
swingFactors: Whether the intermediate success spreads to short throws
Interior line health, starting with Savaiinaea
Hold on the starting job amid an 0-5 start

confidence.note: Five starts, three against top-five defenses, but the profile matches his 2022 season.
